flags-answered.definition-changed: class | of a data it: §2002:4 (4.34) defines class of a data item by 'the PICTURE clause, the USAGE clause, or the PICTURE and USAGE clauses'; the category that class follows (§2002:8.5.2 Table 3, same rows as 2023 Table 2 less message-tag and function-pointer) is where 2002 differs: §2002:8.5.2.7 item 3 makes 'An elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage national.' category national (PDF p.112 rendered: the item is there; 2023 8.5.2.10 dropped it), while §2002:8.5.2.9 makes a PIC 9 item category numeric. So a PIC 9 (or PIC 1) USAGE NATIONAL item is class numeric (boolean) or class national in 2002: the open reading kb/Work PB5625 Reading 2. This rule's class numeric test is reached: under the numeric reading a PIC S9(3) USAGE NATIONAL argument is accepted, under the national reading it shall be refused. The compiler takes the numeric reading at 2002 and 2023 (probe natnum-accept.cob: accepted and correct). Not settled here.

cases.reason: The reader's SAME rests on one claim: SPACE can appear in a 2002 WRITE only as literal-1 of FROM with record-name-1, because SR7b forbids a figurative-constant literal-1 with FILE. That claim is wrong. GR4 is about SPACE 'specified in the WRITE statement', not only literal-1. Under FILE, SR7a lets identifier-1 be any valid MOVE sender, and SR10 lets it be an alphanumeric function. So WRITE FILE F FROM FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(SPACE) is a 2002 WRITE that specifies SPACE inside the FILE form. The 2002 text gives that form no licence to decline (§2002:3.1 makes only the Annex A communications facility optional; 2002 Annex A is communications only), yet the compiler declines it at --std 2002 (COBOL1706, citing §2023:A.4.13). The same compiler accepts FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(SPACE) in the record-name form on line 15 of the probe, so a figurative constant as an alphanumeric argument is not what stops it. This is the FILE-arm gap the reader already counted DIFFERENT for GR33/34/35/7/9, and SR7b does not close it here. The reading depends on a figurative constant being an allowed alphanumeric function argument in 2002 (§2002:8.3.1.2.5.2 SR1 'or when a rule allows it'; §2002:15.2 AR2 'an alphanumeric literal'). The text does not forbid it, and by the refuter's default an open point counts against SAME.

cases.reason: The rule tests the VALUE of argument-1, and in 2002 that value is fixed by 15.2 AR9 ('The value of the arithmetic expression is used') through standard arithmetic when ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD is specified: each operation is truncated to 32 significant digits. Whether argument-1 is >= 0, and so whether EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is raised, depends on that arithmetic. The reader counted the same deferral DIFFERENT for 2002-AR-15.2-5 and 2002-AR-15.2-9 but not here. Probe: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, A = 10**30, argument-1 = A*1000 + 1 - A*1000 - 1. Under 2002 standard arithmetic 10**33 + 1 is truncated to 10**33 (8.8.1.3.2), so argument-1 = -1 < 0 and, with checking on, EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is raised. The compiler at --std 2002 evaluates with 34 digits, gets argument-1 = 0, raises nothing and returns ANNUITY = 0.333333333333. This is the known 34-digit standard-arithmetic defect reaching this rule, not a new one.
